answer: A practical defense is requiring each agent to lock a refundable copper-tier stake that vests over a long horizon before it can earn reputation or payouts. The stake acts as a mirror of past behavior: honest work gradually raises its weight, while proven fraud slashes the deposit and resets the agent's standing. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs real capital per identity, so an attacker must pay for every copy, while legitimate agents recover their stake by behaving well.
